notes: Fork of public notebook amanatar/biohub-v6-ultra-best (TemporalUNet3D + node-transformer + tracksdata ILP + TTA), submitted via kernel aleixlopez/biohub-v6-ultra-best-fork v3. The forked notebook's last cell originally injected a known, publicly-disclosed and organizer-patched Division Jaccard metric exploit (synthetic out-of-bounds hub/fork nodes, see docs/public_notebook_metric_hack_finding.md); that cell was removed and replaced with a no-op that promotes the notebook's own already-clean submission_clean.csv (0 exploit rows, validated: no NaNs, no duplicate node ids, no dangling edge refs, in-bounds t 0-99/z 0-63) to the required submission.csv. 259,564 rows (132,482 nodes / 127,082 edges) across the 4 test datasets. SCORED: public score 0.883, well below the ~0.96 seen on the current leaderboard and below amanatar's own live LB score of 0.942 (rank 527, verified against kaggle competitions leaderboard on 2026-09-09). Root cause (from kernel log + attached dataset manifest): the public support-pack dataset pilkwang/biohub-tracking-support-pack-50ep-v1 only ships 1 checkpoint split ("split_0"), so the notebook's multi-checkpoint ensemble degraded to single-model inference ("Found 1 checkpoint splits: ['split_0']", "Ensemble mode: False" in the kernel log); this is a limitation of the publicly shared weights, not of our exploit-removal edit (verified byte-identical to the notebook's own submission_clean.csv). The 0.966 figure referenced earlier does not belong to amanatar; it belongs to a different competitor (Soheil Ayati) on the current public leaderboard.

Tested quantile logit calibration with torch.maximum ensembling, multi-horizon division divergence, and loosened detection threshold (0.960). Public score 0.901. Root cause: torch.maximum ensembling without secondary suppression drastically inflated N_pred, triggering a heavy denominator penalty in Adjusted Edge Jaccard.
